label: Free 2.0
title: Outcome, correlation id and standard formats
lede: Logarithm 2.0 records how every action ended and ties events of one request together, and it maps events to CloudEvents and OpenTelemetry. Large Postgres tables can now be partitioned, all in the MIT package.

items.title: Outcome: record what was refused
items.text: Every event now says how the action ended: success, failure or denied. Denied attempts are often the first thing an auditor asks about, and you can filter by result.
items.codeTitle: Record a denied export and filter by outcome

items.title: Correlation id across a request
items.text: Set one correlationId per request, job or trace and every event of that operation carries it. Query by it to see everything one request did.
items.codeTitle: Same example: both events share req-7f3a

items.title: CloudEvents 1.0 export
items.text: Turn any event into a CloudEvents envelope for brokers like EventBridge, Event Grid or Knative. The function is pure, so you choose the transport.

items.title: OpenTelemetry logs
items.text: Send events to any OTLP backend such as the OpenTelemetry Collector, Grafana, Datadog or Honeycomb. Severity follows the outcome, and a 32-hex correlation id becomes the trace id.
items.outputTitle: Real output (denied event: severity, body, attributes)
items.output:
WARN export.created
event.name = export.created
enduser.id = u_42
logarithm.event.id = 01M4V049ATC335RY4NRJ6S12NE
logarithm.outcome = denied
logarithm.actor.type = user
logarithm.correlation_id = req-7f3a

items.title: Postgres partitioning
items.text: Very large Postgres audit tables can be partitioned by month or year, so time-range queries stay fast and removing old months is a metadata operation.
items.code:
import { migratePostgres, ensurePartitions } from "@sweberdev/logarithm/postgres"

await migratePostgres({ client: pool, partitioned: true })
await ensurePartitions({ client: pool, from: new Date(), to: "2027-03-31" })
items.outputTitle: Real output of postgresSchema({ partitioned: true }), first lines
items.output:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "audit_events" (
  id text COLLATE "C" NOT NULL,
  occurred_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
  tenant_id text,
  action text NOT NULL,
  actor_id text NOT NULL,
  actor jsonb NOT NULL,
  targets jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
  changes jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
  context jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  metadata jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  outcome text,
  correlation_id text,
  search text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  PRIMARY KEY (occurred_at, id)
) PARTITION BY RANGE (occurred_at);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "audit_events_default" PARTITION OF "audit_events" DEFAULT;

note: Also new in free 2.0: the React ObjectHistory component (history of one object with a diff per change) and a result filter in AuditLog. Existing tables upgrade in place with migrate*; Node 22 or newer is required.
